newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo Bourse hits 10th life high so far this year.
newsitem.headline: Oslo Bourse hits 10th life high so far this year.

text.p: Norwegian shares, boosted by the Wall Street opening, powered to their 10th all-time high so far this year on Friday.
Oslo's Total share index rose 0.39 percent to 1,028.08 points -- the fourth consecutive record close -- in brisk turnover of 1.07 billion crowns.
The index traded sideways for most of the day, but rose in the last hour of the session when U.S. stocks were up a little in early trading.
"If things continue to be alright in the United States we will be doing O.K. next week in Oslo," one dealer said.
"There is some profit-taking," he said. "Norsk Hydro looks worn out. Saga Petroleuym is also falling now because oil prices are not expected to be so high anymore."
Industrial group Hydro, Norway's biggest company, fell 0.4 percent to 363 crowns and was the most traded share at 138 million crowns. Saga shed 1.2 percent to close at 119.50 crowns.
Dealers said metals maker Elkem and Norske Skog, both of which fell, continued to suffer from the strong crown.
But food-based conglomerate Orkla was upbeat, its A share rising 3.07 percent to 504 crowns partly because it is not a major exporter and thus is not hurt by the strong crown.
